beam.description: Long-context memory benchmark: 100 conversations (100K–10M tokens), 2 000 questions across 10 memory ability categories.

lifebench.description: Long-horizon multi-source personalized memory benchmark across 10 users.

locomo.description: Multi-session long-term conversations with 1,986 QA pairs.

locomo10.comment: Self-reported by Plastic Labs. LLM-as-a-judge, deviating from the original paper's F1 methodology; judge model not disclosed. Uses Claude Haiku 4.5 as backbone. Adversarial questions excluded (not mentioned). Scores by category: Single-Hop 84.0%, Multi-Hop 88.2%, Temporal 77.1%, Open-Domain (Commonsense) 93.2%.
Self-reported by MemMachine. LLM-as-a-judge with GPT-4o-mini. Adversarial questions (cat. 5) excluded. Uses gpt-4.1-mini as backbone — stronger LLM directly inflates scores vs. gpt-4o-mini entries.
Self-reported by MemMachine. LLM-as-a-judge with GPT-4o-mini. Adversarial questions (cat. 5) excluded. Uses gpt-4.1-mini as backbone — stronger LLM directly inflates scores vs. gpt-4o-mini entries.

Evaluated by a competitor (MemMachine). LLM-as-a-judge with GPT-4o-mini. Adversarial questions excluded. Uses gpt-4.1-mini backbone — not comparable to the gpt-4o-mini Mem0 entry below.
Self-reported by Letta. LLM-as-a-judge with GPT-4.1 — a stronger judge than the GPT-4o-mini used in MemMachine comparisons, making scores not directly comparable. Adversarial questions excluded.
locomo10.source_label: Letta Blog: Benchmarking AI Agent Memory

locomo-fixed.description: LoComo without the questions its conversations cannot answer (gold answer absent from the conversation, gold contradicting it, or the question naming the wrong person).

hindsight-gemma4.description: Hindsight main bc5ea195a; reflect answers (AMB agent mode); gemma-4-26b-a4b on Hindsight Inference; local embeddings and cross-encoder reranker; recall chunk budget 8k; no consolidation

longmemeval.description: Long-term memory evaluation in LLM-based chat assistants.

s.comment: Reported by the original LongMemEval authors. GPT-4o is used as both the answering and judging model, which may inflate scores compared to evaluations using a separate judge.
Baseline reported in the Zep paper as a reference point, not by the original benchmark authors. Judge model not specified separately.
Older-generation memory system evaluated by a competitor (TiMem). Scores reported by others for MemoryBank are consistently low, suggesting it is not well-suited for this benchmark.
Scores for A-MEM vary widely across papers (55–63%), likely due to sensitivity to LLM backbone and judge configuration. Uses GPT-4o backbone here.
Evaluated by a competitor (TiMem) using GPT-4o as backbone. Only this one paper reports MemoryOS results on LongMemEval.
Scores for Mem0 vary widely across papers (49–68%), likely reflecting different LLM backbones, k-retrieval settings, and judge configurations. Uses GPT-4o backbone here.
Self-reported by Zep authors. Uses GPT-4o as backbone. Zep's graph-based memory gives it an advantage on multi-session and knowledge-update questions.
Self-reported by ENGRAM authors. Uses episodic graph-based memory. LLM backbone not clearly specified in the paper.
Evaluated by a competitor (TiMem) using GPT-4o as backbone. MemOS uses an OS-inspired layered memory architecture.
Self-reported by LiCoMemory authors. Uses GPT-4o-mini as backbone, making this one of the few mid-range-backbone results in this score tier.
Self-reported. Uses GPT-4.1-mini (a newer, more capable model than GPT-4o-mini) as backbone — scores may be higher than GPT-4o-mini baselines suggest.
Self-reported by HyMem authors. Combines multiple memory strategies (hybrid). LLM backbone not clearly specified.
Self-reported. Uses Qwen3-32B (open-source) as backbone, which behaves differently from GPT-4o-family models and makes direct comparison harder.
Self-reported by TiMem authors. Uses GPT-4o as backbone and focuses on temporal-aware memory management.
Only reported in the SmartSearch paper. No self-reported or independent evaluation is available for this score.
Self-reported. Uses GPT-4.1-mini backbone (newer than GPT-4o-mini). 'G' denotes the graph-enhanced variant of EMem.
Self-reported by Memora authors. Uses GPT-4.1-mini backbone. Best of two reported configurations.
Self-reported. Index-free variant (slightly stronger than the indexed variant at 87.6%). Uses GPT-4.1-mini backbone.

Evaluated by a competitor (Hindsight/Vectorize). Uses GPT-4o as backbone. Judge: GPT-OSS-120B — differs from GPT-4o used in the original LongMemEval paper and most other entries here, making direct comparison harder.
Evaluated by a competitor (Hindsight/Vectorize). Uses Gemini-3 Pro Preview as backbone — stronger than GPT-4o, inflating score. Judge: GPT-OSS-120B.

Self-reported by Plastic Labs. LongMemEval S split. LLM-as-a-judge with GPT-4o as judge (following the LongMemEval paper's methodology). Uses Claude Haiku 4.5 as backbone. Score on LongMem M (500 questions): 88.8%. Also reported in the Chronos paper (arXiv:2603.16862).
Reported by the Chronos paper, not self-reported. Best of two configurations tested; the GPT-4o configuration achieved 84.8%. The backbone for this configuration is not specified.

Self-reported by Chronos authors. Best of two configurations tested; the GPT-4o configuration achieved 92.6%. This configuration uses Claude Opus 4.6 as backbone, which is considerably more capable than the models used by most other entries here.

personamem.description: Long-horizon personal preference tracking across conversation sessions.

precisionmembench.description: Belief-level retrieval precision: 77 cases asserting exactly which memories must and must not surface.

hindsight.description: Hindsight 0.10.0 (00caa8eab). Identity and currency labels derived by the extraction LLM (multi-text entity labels); recall filtered server-side via tag_groups with fuzzy tag resolution.

supportbench.description: Does a support agent use the product docs and each customer's history correctly? Real Nextcloud 32 manuals (837 PDF pages) plus per-customer support chats and approved exceptions.

vidore-v3-markdown.description: ViDoRe V3, 8 enterprise PDF tasks (EN + FR) as the page markdown the dataset ships, one text document per page; text-to-page search in 6 query languages.
vidore-v3-markdown.note: nDCG@10 (trec_eval linear gain) over every query of all 6 query languages, against ViDoRe's page-level qrels. The average split is the mean over the 8 tasks, the number Mixedbread's table reports. Search only: no LLM, no reranker, no query rewriting.

hindsight-jev114.description: Hindsight knowledge bank, embeddinggemma-2 search, reranked by Jev 1.14 (TypeSafe System One).

atm-bench-retrieval.description: ATM-Bench as search: 3,759 photos, 533 videos and 6,742 emails (four years of one person's data), 1,013 questions scored on their human-labelled evidence items.
atm-bench-retrieval.note: R@10: the share of a question's evidence items in the top 10 results. Each photo and video goes in as the raw file and as the benchmark's own text record (time, place, caption, OCR, tags); a hit on either counts as the item.

hindsight-jev114.description: Hindsight knowledge bank, embeddinggemma-2 search, reranked by Jev 1.14 (TypeSafe System One).

atm-bench.comment: BGE-M3 + bge-reranker-v2-m3; memory built with DeepSeek (an LLM). R@10 counts the items passed to the answer model.

legalbench-rag.description: LegalBench-RAG mini: 776 questions over 714 contracts (NDAs, M&A agreements, commercial contracts, privacy policies), scored on the exact characters lawyers marked.
legalbench-rag.note: Character recall@5, as legalbenchrag/run_benchmark.py computes it: the share of the marked characters that the top 5 results' text covers. The 4 sets weigh the same (194 questions each). The search runs at the API's default budget of 4,096 tokens, so the 5 results carry about as much text as 5 chunks of a typical RAG setup. Precision (the share of returned text that is marked) is in each query's metrics. Documents go in with neutral names. Search only: no LLM.

hindsight-pr6704.description: Hindsight knowledge bank (PR #6704): embeddinggemma-2 search, 512-token passages, one rerank by hs-decide-1-flash-mm judging each passage alone, fused with the search order of documents. Contracts under neutral ids, no file names (as Conare ran it).
